title: Program audits convert broad field promises into accountable scope
summary: This provisional pattern candidate links ALPAC and Lighthill as program-audit records: formal evaluators assess broad promises, find that near-term or general claims exceed demonstrated capability, and redirect attention toward narrower, accountable work. Dartmouth 1956 supplies upstream AI founding-promise context, not negative evidence. The pattern is intentionally fragile until negative controls and downstream consequence records are added.

status_history.note: No program-audit pattern existed before the genealogy/audit pass.
Promoted as candidate only from ALPAC, Lighthill, and Dartmouth context records.

place.scope: US machine-translation research-policy context and UK AI research-policy context; cross-national comparison not yet complete

claims.claim: ALPAC and Lighthill are enough to seed a candidate pattern in which a research program’s broad promise was forced into accountable scope by a formal evaluator/audit report, while the Dartmouth record supplies upstream founding-promise context for AI.
what_would_change_status: Negative controls show that the pattern is too broad.
Downstream causal histories show one or both audit records are misclassified.

claims.claim: Program-audit records should keep the audited promise, evaluator mandate, negative finding, preserved/recommended work, downstream funding/practice consequences, and historiographic cautions as separate fields.
what_would_change_status: Later program-audit records require a different schema or show these fields are redundant.

Lighthill record needs report text, response scene, and causal caution

limitations: Two audit cases are insufficient for a mature pattern.

type_payload.candidate_rule: When a research program makes broad practical or field-defining promises, a formal evaluator may force scope separation: what has been demonstrated, what remains conjectural, what narrower research should continue, and what policy/funding consequence follows.
provisional_mechanisms: evaluator mandate converts diffuse optimism into explicit criteria
hard endpoint or practical-performance test exposes gap between demonstration and useful deployment
preserved-research recommendations prevent negative result from becoming blanket rejection
public/policy reception can overcompress the audit into a slogan
scope_cautions: Not a claim that evaluator reports are always right.
Not mature until positive controls and negative controls exist.
Modern success can be historically compatible with earlier negative program audits if capabilities, data, compute, evaluation, and use cases changed.
negative_controls_needed: program audits that found promise and were later vindicated
program audits that were wrong or prematurely pessimistic
programs with broad promise but no formal audit
audits that redirected work without causing funding contraction
type_payload.maturity_gate: Requires at least five audited-program records, two positive/negative controls, and a downstream-consequence review before synthesis promotion.

positive_controls_needed: Add another formal program audit where a broad research-program promise was narrowed by evaluator evidence while narrower work remained valid.
negative_controls_needed: Add a program audit that was later judged too pessimistic or methodologically weak.
counterexamples_to_seek: A broad program promise that survived independent audit and achieved its original scope.
rollback_triggers: A second-review extraction demotes or materially weakens one of the support records.
A negative-control record shows the pattern label fits too many unrelated cases.
A counterexample shows the claimed recurrence is better explained by a narrower or different mechanism.
The pattern is upgraded only after controls and not by record count alone.
red_team_controls.split_or_merge_watch: Medium: program-audit records may split into funding-governance, technical-feasibility, and disciplinary-boundary subpatterns.

maturity_gate.minimum_before_mature: At least one positive control, at least one negative control, an explicit counterexample search, and a rollback/split decision recorded in the claim-status ledger.

links.note: Both preserve promise-route, hard test/audit, and scope cautions rather than binary failure labels.

handling_notes: Do not weaponize evaluator reports against fields or people.
Include revival and correction stories in later records.

unknowns: Causal strength for funding and practice changes
next_actions: Add an explicit AI winter synthesis candidate with source-backed funding timeline.

Add at least one negative-control or counterexample record before upgrading this pattern beyond candidate level.
